summary: Recorded a source-based correction note rather than a durable Fact revision: the earlier snapshot-trigger Fact's consequence sentence implied a per-interval recurrence that the measurement did not support, and the stored-snapshot count I used to gauge repetition was shown by source not to track snapshot attempts (the in-memory snapshot store replaces its single latest snapshot on Create and List returns only that one, while the file-backed store reaps older snapshots by its retain count). The evidenced consequence is now stated as witnessed redundant snapshot creation at the unchanged index with an unmeasured rate, on top of the persistent spurious verdict (store_last=0 against snapshot_index=3 with applied_index=3 and should_snapshot=true, CheckRun a4a0cbfa094b4d1982032d9de0652861, sustained through later samples). Attempting to revise the Fact under its existing id was rejected twice by validation - a knowledge update may not carry a revision field and its affected-use reference must be revision-qualified - so this cycle records the correction in the update and leaves the Fact text untouched, with the correction ready to be carried into the Fact under its own id in a later update. This changes no verdict: the asserted defect, its bound to redundant snapshot work with no safety effect, and its limitations stand.
